en: to be paralyzed during a nightmare

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 가위눌려서 한참 동안 움직일 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I had sleep paralysis last night and couldn't move for a long time.
When I'm tired, I often get sleep paralysis.
I often had sleep paralysis when I was little.
If you get sleep paralysis, try moving your fingers first.

examples.ko: 무서운 영화를 보고 자면 가위눌릴까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: If I sleep after watching a scary movie, I worry I'll get sleep paralysis.

examples.ko: 가위눌려도 무서워하지 말고 숨을 천천히 쉬어 보세요.
examples.en: Even if you get sleep paralysis, don't be scared; try breathing slowly.

explain: 자다가 몸이 안 움직이고 숨이 막히는 것 같은 경험을 말해요. '가위에 눌리다'라고도 하고 둘 다 자주 써요. 보통 '자다가 가위눌렸어요'처럼 잠잘 때 일어난 일에 말해요.
explain_en: It describes the experience of not being able to move and feeling like you can't breathe while sleeping. People also say '가위에 눌리다', and both forms are common. You usually use it for something that happened during sleep, as in '자다가 가위눌렸어요'.

examples.ko: 저는 손을 자주 씻는 강박증이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a compulsion to wash my hands often.

examples.ko: 강박증 때문에 문을 몇 번씩 확인해요.
examples.en: Because of my obsessive-compulsive tendency, I check the door several times.

examples.ko: 강박증은 치료를 받으면 좋아질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Obsessive-compulsive disorder can get better with treatment.
I'm suffering from a compulsion to be perfect.

examples.ko: 강박증을 이겨 내려고 상담을 받기 시작했어요.
examples.en: I started counseling to overcome my compulsion.

examples.ko: 청소 강박증처럼 보이지만 단순한 습관일 수도 있어요.
examples.en: It looks like a cleaning compulsion, but it might just be a habit.

explain: 어떤 생각이나 행동을 안 하면 불안해서 계속 반복하게 되는 마음의 어려움을 말해요. 병원이나 상담 이야기에서 쓰고, 친구끼리는 가볍게 '나 강박증 있나 봐'라고도 해요. 진단과 관련된 말이라 다른 사람에게 함부로 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It refers to a condition where you feel anxious unless you repeat certain thoughts or actions. It is used in medical and counseling contexts, and friends sometimes joke '나 강박증 있나 봐'. Because it relates to diagnosis, it's best not to say it carelessly about other people.

en: to be rough; to be bumpy; to be knotty

examples.en: In winter my hands get rough from the cold wind.

examples.ko: 자고 일어나니 얼굴이 거칠거칠해서 팩을 붙였어요.
examples.en: My face felt rough when I woke up, so I put on a face mask.

examples.ko: 이 수건은 너무 거칠거칠한 느낌이라 싫어요.
examples.en: This towel feels too rough, so I don't like it.

examples.ko: 벽이 거칠거칠하니까 손으로 함부로 만지지 마세요.
examples.en: The wall is rough, so please don't touch it carelessly with your hands.

examples.ko: 사포질을 했는데도 나무 표면이 아직 거칠거칠하네요.
examples.en: Even after sanding, the wood surface is still rough.
When my lips get rough, I always put on some cream.

explain: '거칠다'는 성격, 말투, 파도 등에도 두루 쓰지만, '거칠거칠하다'는 손이나 피부, 종이, 벽처럼 만졌을 때의 까칠한 느낌에 주로 써요. 반대로 매끈하고 부드러운 느낌은 '매끈매끈하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '거칠다' covers many things such as personality, speech and waves, but '거칠거칠하다' is mostly about the rough feel of skin, paper or walls when you touch them. The opposite smooth feel is '매끈매끈하다'.

en: to stand on end; to bristle up

examples.en: My hair stood on end while I was watching a scary movie.

examples.ko: 시험 전날에는 신경이 곤두서서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The night before the exam I was so on edge that I couldn't sleep.
When a cat gets scared, the fur on its back bristles.

examples.ko: 그 소리를 들으니 온몸의 털이 곤두서는 느낌이었어요.
examples.en: Hearing that sound, I felt every hair on my body stand up.

examples.ko: 요즘 일이 많아서 다들 신경이 곤두서 있어요.
examples.en: There is so much work these days that everyone is on edge.
It was so scary that my hair stood on end.

explain: 머리카락, 털, 신경처럼 가늘고 예민한 것에 많이 써요. 일부러 세울 때는 '곤두세우다'를 써서 '귀를 곤두세우다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 발표 전에는 신경이 곤두서서 아무것도 못 먹었어요.
phrases.en: Before the presentation I was so on edge that I couldn't eat anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 긴장이나 스트레스 때문에 작은 일에도 예민해진 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes being tense and oversensitive to small things because of stress.

explain_en: It is mostly used for thin, sensitive things like hair, fur and nerves. When you raise something on purpose, use '곤두세우다', as in '귀를 곤두세우다' (to prick up one's ears).

examples.ko: 갑자기 놀란 고양이의 꼬리가 위로 곧추섰어요.
examples.en: The startled cat's tail suddenly shot straight up.

examples.ko: 의자에 앉을 때 허리가 곧추서면 덜 피곤해요.
examples.en: If your back is upright when you sit, you get less tired.
The soldiers saluted in an upright posture.
The blades of grass are standing upright in the morning sun.
Even when I try to stand up straight, my legs have no strength.

examples.ko: 몸이 곧추서야 노래할 때 소리가 잘 나와요.
examples.en: Your voice comes out well when singing only if your body is upright.

explain: 몸, 허리, 꼬리처럼 세로로 곧게 서는 것에 써요. 그냥 '서다'보다 꼿꼿한 느낌이 있어요. 내가 일부러 세울 때는 '곧추세우다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used for things that stand straight up vertically, such as the body, back or tail. It feels more rigid than plain '서다'. When you make something stand on purpose, use '곧추세우다'.

examples.en: He was shocked and his face turned white.

examples.ko: 무서운 얘기를 들은 듯 낯빛에 두려움이 가득했어요.
examples.en: Her face was full of fear, as if she had heard something frightening.

examples.ko: 어머니는 내 낯빛을 보고 무슨 일이 있다는 걸 아셨어요.
examples.en: My mother saw the look on my face and knew something was wrong.

examples.ko: 밤새 일했더니 낯빛도 어둡고 기운도 없어요.
examples.en: After working all night, my complexion is dull and I have no energy.

examples.ko: 선생님은 낯빛 하나 바꾸지 않고 차분하게 대답하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher answered calmly without changing expression at all.

examples.ko: 낯빛으로 보아 시험을 잘 본 것 같아요.
examples.en: Judging by the look on his face, he seems to have done well on the exam.

explain: '안색'과 비슷하지만 '낯빛'이 더 순우리말 느낌이고, '안색'은 좀 더 격식 있게 들려요. 건강뿐 아니라 놀람, 기쁨 같은 감정이 얼굴에 드러난 모습도 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '안색', but '낯빛' feels more native Korean while '안색' sounds a bit more formal. It covers not only health but also emotions such as surprise or joy showing on the face.

examples.en: I fell and got internal bleeding in my leg.

examples.ko: 머리를 세게 부딪히면 내출혈로 이어질 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you hit your head hard, it could lead to internal bleeding.
The doctor suspected internal bleeding and recommended a test.
I got a big bruise because of internal bleeding.

examples.ko: 사고 후에 내출혈 여부를 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: After an accident, you need to check whether there is internal bleeding.

examples.ko: 내출혈을 막으려고 약을 조심해서 먹고 있어요.
examples.en: I am taking my medicine carefully to prevent internal bleeding.

explain: 몸속에서 피가 나는 것이고, 피가 몸 밖으로 나오는 '외출혈'과 짝이에요. 겉으로는 안 보여서 사고 뒤에 병원에서 확인하는 경우가 많아요. 멍도 피부 아래에서 피가 나서 생기는 거라 작은 내출혈과 비슷해요.
explain_en: It means bleeding inside the body, and it pairs with '외출혈', where blood comes out of the body. Because it cannot be seen from outside, it is often checked at a hospital after an accident. A bruise also comes from bleeding under the skin, so it is similar to a small internal bleed.

en: decrepitude; infirmity of old age; senility

examples.ko: 나이가 들면 몸의 노쇠는 누구나 피할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Once you get older, the decline of the body is something no one can avoid.

examples.ko: 의사가 할머니의 건강 문제는 병이 아니라 노쇠 때문이라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said Grandma's health problem is not a disease but due to old age.

examples.ko: 노쇠를 늦추려면 꾸준히 운동하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: To slow down aging, it is good to exercise regularly.

examples.ko: 이 연구는 세포의 노쇠 과정을 알아보는 거예요.
examples.en: This study looks into the process of cell aging.

examples.ko: 감독은 선수의 노쇠가 눈에 띄자 교체를 결정했어요.
examples.en: When the player's decline became noticeable, the coach decided to replace him.

examples.ko: 강아지도 노쇠로 눈이 잘 안 보이게 돼요.
examples.en: Dogs, too, lose their eyesight because of old age.

explain: '늙음'보다 딱딱한 말이고, 늙어서 몸과 기운이 약해지는 점에 초점이 있어요. 사람뿐 아니라 동물이나 세포에도 쓰고 뉴스나 의학 설명에서 많이 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '늙다', '기력이 떨어지다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is a stiffer word than '늙음' (being old) and focuses on the body and strength weakening with age. It is used for people, animals and cells, and appears in news and medical explanations. In everyday talk people say '늙다' or '기력이 떨어지다'.

examples.ko: 나이가 들면서 노안이 와서 안경을 새로 맞췄어요.
examples.en: As I got older I developed presbyopia, so I got new glasses.

examples.ko: 노안 때문에 작은 글씨가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: Because of age-related eyesight, small print is hard to see.

examples.ko: 아버지는 노안으로 책을 멀리 두고 보세요.
examples.en: My father holds books far away to read because of aging eyes.

examples.ko: 노안은 보통 마흔 살 넘어서 시작돼요.
examples.en: Age-related eyesight loss usually begins after forty.

examples.ko: 노안 렌즈로 바꾸니 스마트폰 보기가 편해졌어요.
examples.en: After changing to presbyopia lenses, it got easier to read my phone.
I'm worried that I might have aging eyes too.

explain: 근시는 먼 곳이 흐릿하고, 노안은 나이가 들어 가까운 곳이 흐릿해지는 증상이에요. '노안이 오다', '노안이 시작되다'처럼 써요. 안경 가게에서는 '돋보기'나 '다초점 렌즈' 이야기와 함께 나와요.
explain_en: Nearsightedness blurs distant things, while '노안' blurs things up close as you age. Say '노안이 오다' or '노안이 시작되다'. At an optician it comes up along with '돋보기' and '다초점 렌즈'.

examples.en: Skin ages as you get older.
The doctor said my eyes aged early.
When cells age, the body weakens.
The speed of aging differs for each person.

examples.ko: 운동을 안 하면 몸이 더 빨리 노화할 거예요.
examples.en: If you don't exercise, your body will age faster.
You look aged in the face from heavy stress.

explain: 사람이나 몸의 기능이 나이 들어 약해지는 것을 과학적으로 말해요. 일상에서는 '늙다', '나이 들다'가 더 자연스러워요. 주어는 보통 '피부', '세포', '몸'처럼 몸이나 부분이에요.
explain_en: It describes the body or its functions weakening with age in a scientific tone. In daily speech 늙다 or 나이 들다 is more natural. The subject is usually the body or a part of it, such as skin or cells.

examples.en: My uncle was diagnosed with a brain tumor and had surgery.

examples.ko: 뇌종양은 증상이 사람마다 다르게 나타날 수 있어요.
examples.en: The symptoms of a brain tumor can differ from person to person.
My headaches kept coming, so I even got tested for a brain tumor.

examples.ko: 뇌종양으로 투병하는 친구를 위해 모금 행사에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a fundraiser for a friend battling a brain tumor.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 뇌종양의 증상을 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor explained the symptoms of a brain tumor.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 뇌종양을 이겨 내고 다시 무대에 섰어요.
examples.en: That actor overcame a brain tumor and returned to the stage.

explain: '종양'은 몸에 생긴 혹 같은 덩어리이고, 양성인 것도 있고 악성(암)인 것도 있어요. 그래서 '뇌종양'이라고 해서 모두 뇌암은 아니에요. '뇌종양 진단/수술/환자'처럼 병원 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '종양' is a lump-like mass in the body, and it can be benign or malignant (cancer). So a '뇌종양' is not always brain cancer. It comes up in medical talk, as in '뇌종양 진단/수술/환자'.

en: to pull low one's hat or cap

examples.en: I pulled my hat down low and went out.
I pulled my cap down deep to hide my face.

examples.ko: 야구 모자를 눌러쓴 남자가 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: A man with his baseball cap pulled low looked at me.
It's cold, so I pull my wool hat down over my ears.
If I pull my hat down in the morning, my hair gets flattened.
It was raining, so I pulled my raincoat hood down low.

explain: 모자 같은 것을 깊이 내려서 쓸 때 쓰고, 보통 '푹'과 잘 어울려요. 글씨를 힘주어 꾹꾹 쓸 때도 '눌러쓰다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when you pull a hat or similar item down low, often with '푹'. It is also used for writing with firm pressure, pressing hard on the paper.

examples.ko: 동생이 거짓말을 하자 엄마가 도끼눈으로 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: When my sister lied, Mom glared at her.
Please don't glare at me like that.

examples.ko: 친구가 도끼눈을 하고 저를 노려봐서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: My friend glared at me with sharp eyes, and it was scary.
They asked in an accusing glare, so it was hard to answer.
My boss checked the documents with a sharp, stern look.

examples.ko: 아이들이 도끼눈을 한 채 서로 눈치를 봤어요.
examples.en: The kids eyed each other with glaring looks.

explain: 화가 나거나 미워서 눈을 모나게 뜨고 볼 때 쓰는 말이에요. '도끼눈을 뜨다', '도끼눈으로 보다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '째려보다'가 있는데, 도끼눈은 표정과 눈매를 그릴 때 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: This describes eyes opened sharply in anger or dislike, used as '도끼눈을 뜨다' or '도끼눈으로 보다'. '째려보다' is similar, but 도끼눈 sounds more natural when describing the look on someone's face.

en: the lower part of the nape

examples.en: The back of my neck suddenly felt chilly, so I looked behind me.
The teacher grabbed the child who was messing around by the back of the neck.
The back of my neck got bright red from the sun at the beach.
The back of my neck is stiff, so I want to get a massage.
The cat carried its kitten by the scruff of the neck.
With my hair tied up high, the back of my neck feels cool.

explain: 목 뒤쪽 아래 부분이에요. '목덜미'라고도 하는데, 일상에서는 둘 다 자주 써요. '뒷덜미를 잡다/잡히다'는 비유로도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 몰래 숙제를 베끼다가 선생님께 뒷덜미를 잡혔어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못이나 약점이 들켜서 붙잡히거나 꼼짝 못 하게 되는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a mistake or weak point is discovered and you are caught or cornered.

explain_en: It is the lower back part of the neck, and it is also called '목덜미'; both are common in daily speech. '뒷덜미를 잡다/잡히다' is also widely used figuratively.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 들창코라서 웃을 때 더 귀여워요.
examples.en: My little brother has an upturned nose, so he looks even cuter when he smiles.
I was teased for having an upturned nose when I was little.
Piglets have such cute snub noses.
I take after my dad, so I have an upturned nose too.
That actor is popular even though he has an upturned nose.
That puppy has a snub nose and round eyes.

explain: '매부리코', '납작코'처럼 코 모양을 가리키는 말 중 하나예요. 귀엽다는 느낌으로 말하기도 하지만, 남의 외모를 말할 때는 놀리는 말로 들릴 수 있으니 조심해요.
explain_en: It is one of several words for nose shapes, like '매부리코' (hooked nose) and '납작코' (flat nose). Some people say it affectionately as cute, but it can sound like teasing when you talk about someone's looks, so be careful.

en: to be dim; to be faint; to be vague

examples.en: I stayed up all night, so my head feels foggy.

examples.ko: 감기약을 먹은 뒤에 정신이 몽롱해서 계속 졸았어요.
examples.en: After taking cold medicine, my mind was hazy and I kept dozing off.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나면 한동안 몽롱한 상태로 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: When I wake up in the morning, I sit there in a daze for a while.
The foggy dawn road looked hazy and dreamlike.

examples.ko: 몽롱하지 않으려고 아침에 커피를 한 잔 마셨어요.
examples.en: I had a cup of coffee in the morning so I wouldn't feel groggy.

examples.ko: 꿈에서 막 깬 것처럼 한참 몽롱했어요.
examples.en: I felt dazed for a long while, as if I had just woken from a dream.

explain: 졸리거나 아파서 정신이 흐릿할 때 써요. '멍하다'는 생각 없이 가만히 있는 느낌이고, '몽롱하다'는 반쯤 잠든 듯 의식이 흐린 느낌이에요. 안개나 불빛처럼 분위기가 흐릿하고 꿈같을 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when your mind is blurry from sleepiness or illness. '멍하다' means spacing out with an empty mind, while '몽롱하다' feels like being half asleep with clouded awareness. It can also describe hazy, dreamlike scenes such as fog or soft lights.

en: to be bald; to be hairless

examples.ko: 머리를 너무 짧게 깎아서 머리가 민숭민숭해요.
examples.en: I cut my hair so short that my head looks bare.
The top of my father's head is getting thinner and thinner.
There's no grass, so the hill looks bare.
I shaved my beard clean so my chin is smooth.
The baby's head is still bare.
The mountain with all its trees cut down looks bare.

explain: 머리카락, 수염, 풀, 나무처럼 있어야 할 것이 없어서 반반하게 드러난 모습이에요. 머리, 턱, 산, 언덕 같은 곳에 써요. 비슷한 말로 '맨송맨송하다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a surface that looks smooth and exposed because something expected, such as hair, a beard, grass or trees, is missing. It is used for heads, chins, mountains and hills. '맨송맨송하다' is a similar word.

en: to be slippery; to be sleek

examples.en: I put oil on my hair, and now it's glossy.
My newly bought shoes are shining sleekly.
Don't be fooled by his slick way of talking.
The fur looks glossy and shiny.
I ate oily food, so my lips were shiny.
It's only shiny on the outside; it's empty inside.

explain: 윤기가 나고 매끈해 보일 때 써요. '번지르르하다'와 모음만 다른 비슷한 말로, 반지르르가 조금 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요. '겉만 반지르르하다'처럼 겉모습만 좋은 것을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Use it for something that looks shiny and smooth. It is a close relative of '번지르르하다' differing only in vowels, with 반지르르 feeling a bit smaller and lighter. It is also used for things that only look good outside, as in '겉만 반지르르하다'.

examples.ko: 배란이 규칙적이지 않아서 병원에서 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: My ovulation isn't regular, so I got tested at the hospital.

examples.ko: 배란일을 계산해 주는 앱을 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm using an app that calculates my ovulation day.

examples.ko: 배란 시기에는 몸이 조금 피곤할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Around ovulation, your body can feel a bit tired.

examples.ko: 배란 후에는 체온이 약간 올라간다고 해요.
examples.en: They say body temperature rises slightly after ovulation.

examples.ko: 스트레스를 많이 받으면 배란이 늦어질 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard ovulation can be delayed when you're under a lot of stress.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 배란 주기를 기록해 보라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to keep a record of my ovulation cycle.

explain: '배란일', '배란기', '배란 주기'처럼 다른 말과 붙여서 자주 써요. 건강 검진이나 임신 준비, 생리 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '배란이 되다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is often combined with other words, as in '배란일', '배란기' and '배란 주기'. It comes up in health checkups, talk about trying to conceive, and menstrual cycles. People usually say '배란이 되다'.

examples.en: I was so embarrassed that my face turned red.

examples.ko: 매운 걸 먹으면 얼굴이 금방 벌게져요.
examples.en: My face quickly turns red when I eat spicy food.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 코가 벌게졌어요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day and my nose turned red.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 귀까지 벌게진 채 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: He shouted with his ears red with anger.

examples.ko: 햇볕에 오래 있었더니 팔이 벌게져서 따가워요.
examples.en: I was in the sun for a long time and my arm is red and stinging.
I cried for a long time until my eyes were red.

explain: 부끄러움, 화, 추위, 햇볕 때문에 얼굴이나 피부가 붉어질 때 써요. '빨개지다'보다 어둡고 탁한 붉은색 느낌이에요. '벌겋다'가 기본형 형용사이고 '벌게지다'는 그렇게 변하는 과정을 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when the face or skin turns red from embarrassment, anger, cold or sun. The red feels darker and duller than with '빨개지다'. '벌겋다' is the adjective, and '벌게지다' describes the change into that color.

examples.en: He looks so sickly that I'm worried.
I put on makeup to hide how sick I looked.
He doesn't look ill, but he seems to have no energy.
He came to work with a sickly-looking face.
After resting a few days, the sickly look has mostly gone too.

examples.ko: 친구의 병색에 놀라서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was so shocked at my friend's sickly look that I couldn't say a word.

explain: '병색이 짙다', '병색이 있다', '병색이 가시다'처럼 써요. 몸이 안 좋아 보이는 얼굴빛을 말해서, 일상에서는 '안색이 안 좋다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It appears as '병색이 짙다', '병색이 있다' or '병색이 가시다'. It describes a face that looks unwell, and in daily talk people also say '안색이 안 좋다'.

examples.en: My strength declined as I got older.
My grandfather's health has weakened, so he goes out less.

examples.ko: 한때 강했던 나라도 힘이 쇠하는 때가 와요.
examples.en: Even a once-strong country has a time when its power fades.
My eyesight is gradually getting worse, so I changed my glasses.

examples.ko: 병을 앓고 나서 체력이 많이 쇠했나 봐요.
examples.en: I guess my stamina dropped a lot after being ill.

examples.ko: 쇠해 가는 마을에 젊은 사람들이 돌아오고 있어요.
examples.en: Young people are coming back to the declining village.

explain: 기운, 힘, 세력이 약해질 때 써요. 반대말은 '흥하다'나 '성하다'예요. 보통 '기력이 쇠하다', '체력이 쇠하다'처럼 몸이나 힘 이야기에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when energy, strength or influence grows weaker. Its opposites are '흥하다' and '성하다'. It often appears in phrases about the body or strength, such as '기력이 쇠하다' and '체력이 쇠하다'.

examples.en: I hurt my Achilles tendon while running.
My Achilles tendon was strained, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 운동하기 전에 아킬레스건을 충분히 풀어 주세요.
examples.en: Stretch your Achilles tendon well before exercising.
English pronunciation is my Achilles' heel.
That company's Achilles' heel is its lack of technology.

examples.ko: 상대 팀은 우리의 아킬레스건을 정확히 알고 공격했어요.
examples.en: The other team knew our weak point exactly and attacked it.

explain: 발뒤꿈치 위의 힘줄이라는 뜻 외에, 비유로 '가장 치명적인 약점'을 말해요. '약점'과 비슷하지만 전체를 흔들 수 있는 가장 큰 약점이라는 느낌이 강해요. 몸 이야기인지 비유인지는 문맥으로 구분해요.
explain_en: Besides the tendon above the heel, it figuratively means one's most critical weakness. It is close to '약점' but suggests the biggest weak spot that could bring everything down. Context tells you whether it is about the body or a metaphor.

examples.en: I had surgery before the cancer cells spread.
The test showed there were no cancer cells.

examples.ko: 의사들은 암세포만 없애는 약을 연구하고 있어요.
examples.en: Doctors are researching a drug that destroys only cancer cells.
The new treatment attacks cancer cells.

examples.ko: 암세포의 크기가 작아져서 치료가 잘 되고 있대요.
examples.en: I heard the cancer cells have shrunk, so the treatment is going well.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 암세포를 찾는 인공지능 기술을 소개했어요.
examples.en: The news introduced AI technology that finds cancer cells.

explain: 병원 이야기에서 '암세포가 퍼지다', '암세포가 없어지다'처럼 쓰고, 보통 대화에서는 그냥 '암'이라고 짧게 말해요. 가까운 사람의 병 이야기는 조심스럽게 꺼내는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: In medical talk you say '암세포가 퍼지다' or '암세포가 없어지다', while in normal conversation people usually just say '암'. It is best to bring up a close person's illness carefully.

en: to become thin; to lose weight

examples.ko: 병을 앓고 나서 얼굴이 많이 여위었어요.
examples.en: After being ill, her face became very thin.

examples.ko: 요즘 밥을 못 먹어서 점점 여위어 가요.
examples.en: I can't eat these days, so I'm growing thinner.
Seeing his thin shoulders made my heart ache.
Grandmother has grown so thin that I'm worried.
The cat was thin, but its eyes were bright.
You look worn thin because of hard work.

explain: 병이나 고생 때문에 몸이 마르고 약해 보일 때 써서, 날씬해졌다는 칭찬과 달리 걱정하는 느낌이 있어요. 활용은 '여위어요, 여위었어요, 여윈'으로 해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone gets thin and looks frail from illness or hardship, so it carries a worried feeling, unlike a compliment about being slim. The forms are '여위어요, 여위었어요, 여윈'.

examples.en: The baby eats baby food, working its mouth.
The hamster nibbles on a sunflower seed.
Grandmother said something, moving her lips.
The child put candy in its mouth and rolled it around.
The way the rabbit nibbles on grass is cute.

examples.ko: 입안에서 오물거리지 말고 크게 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't mumble in your mouth; speak up.

explain: 작은 입을 계속 움직이며 씹거나 말할 때 써서 귀엽고 작은 느낌이 있어요. '우물거리다'도 비슷하지만 더 크고 불분명하게 움직이는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when a small mouth keeps moving as it chews or talks, with a cute, small feel. '우물거리다' is similar but feels bigger and less clear.

examples.en: After a good rest, I got my energy back.
After taking a tonic, my vitality recovered a lot.
My grandmother is still full of vigor.

examples.ko: 몸살을 앓고 나서 원기도 없고 입맛도 없어요.
examples.en: After being sick with body aches, I have no energy and no appetite.
I heard this food is good for restoring vitality.
The children greeted us in voices full of energy.

explain: 몸의 기운을 말해서 아프거나 지친 뒤 회복하는 이야기, 나이 드신 분의 건강 이야기에 잘 나와요. '원기를 회복하다', '원기 왕성하다'처럼 짝으로 익혀 두세요. 평소 말에서는 '기운'이라고 더 많이 해요.
explain_en: It refers to physical energy and often comes up when talking about recovering after illness or fatigue, or about the health of elderly people. Learn it in set pairs like '원기를 회복하다' and '원기 왕성하다'. In everyday speech people more often say '기운'.

en: manic depressive disorder; manic depression; bipolar disorder

examples.ko: 그는 조울증 진단을 받고 꾸준히 치료받고 있어요.
examples.en: He was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and is getting steady treatment.

examples.ko: 조울증 때문에 약을 먹는 친구를 이해해 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to understand my friend who takes medication for bipolar disorder.

examples.ko: 조울증이 있어도 규칙적인 생활이 도움이 된대요.
examples.en: They say a regular routine helps even if you have bipolar disorder.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 조울증에 대해 자세히 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor explained bipolar disorder to me in detail.

examples.ko: 조울증을 앓는 사람들에게는 가족의 지지가 중요해요.
examples.en: Family support is important for people living with bipolar disorder.

examples.ko: 드라마 주인공이 조울증으로 힘들어하는 모습이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The drama showed the main character struggling with bipolar disorder.

explain: 의학 용어라서 병원, 뉴스, 건강 이야기에서 쓰고, 요즘은 '양극성 장애'라는 말도 같이 써요. 기분이 오르락내리락하는 사람을 놀리듯 '너 조울증이야?'라고 가볍게 말하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a medical term used in hospitals, news and health talk, and '양극성 장애' is also used these days. Casually teasing someone with a mood swing by saying '너 조울증이야?' can be rude.

examples.ko: 최면에 걸린 사람은 시키는 대로 행동하기도 해요.
examples.en: A person under hypnosis sometimes acts as told.

examples.ko: 그는 최면 치료로 불안한 마음을 다스렸어요.
examples.en: He calmed his anxiety with hypnotherapy.
I talked myself into doing my homework.

examples.ko: 최면이 풀리자 그는 아무것도 기억하지 못했어요.
examples.en: When the hypnosis wore off, he couldn't remember anything.
Hypnosis is also a field studied scientifically.

examples.ko: 최면에서 깨어난 사람은 졸린 듯 눈을 비볐어요.
examples.en: The person who woke from hypnosis rubbed his eyes as if sleepy.

explain: '최면을 걸다', '최면에 걸리다', '최면이 풀리다'처럼 동사와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 실제 최면뿐 아니라 '자기 최면'처럼 스스로 그렇다고 믿으려 할 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 비유로 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.example: 이번에는 잘할 수 있다고 스스로에게 최면을 걸었어요.
phrases.en: I talked myself into believing I could do well this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 최면이 아니라 마음속으로 계속 그렇다고 믿으려 하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It isn't real hypnosis; it means repeatedly trying to make yourself believe something.
phrases.en_equiv: talk oneself into it; psych oneself up

explain_en: It is often used with verbs, as in '최면을 걸다', '최면에 걸리다' and '최면이 풀리다'. Besides real hypnosis, it is used for trying to make yourself believe something, as in '자기 최면'. In daily conversation you hear the figurative use more often.

examples.ko: 임신 오 개월쯤 되니 태동이 느껴져요.
examples.en: At about five months of pregnancy, I can feel the baby moving.

examples.ko: 처음 태동을 느꼈을 때 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: I cried when I felt the baby move for the first time.

examples.ko: 아기 태동은 사람마다 느끼는 시기가 달라요.
examples.en: The time when you feel the baby move differs from person to person.
The baby's movements kept waking me up at dawn.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 태동 검사를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor did a fetal movement test for me.
I was startled by a sudden kick and called my husband.

explain: 배 속의 아기가 움직이는 것을 말해요. 임신과 병원 이야기에서 '태동이 느껴지다', '태동 검사'처럼 써요. 글에서는 새로운 움직임이나 시대가 막 시작되는 것을 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: It means the movement of the baby in the womb. It is used in pregnancy and hospital talk, as in '태동이 느껴지다' or '태동 검사'. In writing it is also used figuratively for a new movement or era just beginning to stir.

examples.en: These pants are loose around the waist, so they're comfortable.
I stayed home wearing a baggy T-shirt.

examples.ko: 이 치마 입으면 엉덩이가 펑퍼짐해 보이지 않아요?
examples.en: Doesn't my hip look wide when I wear this skirt?
That dress is too baggy.
As I got older, my figure became broader and rounder.

examples.ko: 옷을 펑퍼짐하게 입으면 더 커 보여요.
examples.en: If you wear baggy clothes, you look bigger.

explain: 옷이 헐렁하고 넉넉할 때, 또 엉덩이나 몸이 옆으로 넓고 둥글게 퍼져 있을 때 써요. 사람의 몸에 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있으니 남에게는 조심해서 말해요.
explain_en: It describes clothes that are loose and roomy, or a body or hips that spread wide and round. Using it about someone's body can be rude, so be careful when talking about other people.

en: to be weak; to be fragile; to be feeble

examples.en: I was physically frail as a child.
Grandma has become frail these days.
Sometimes people give herbal tonic to a frail child.
My stamina is weak, so it's hard to walk for long.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 수비가 허약해서 자주 져요.
examples.en: That team's defense is weak, so they lose often.

examples.ko: 허약하지 않으려면 운동을 꾸준히 해야 해요.
examples.en: To not be frail, you need to exercise steadily.

explain: 사람의 몸이 약해 쉽게 아플 때 써요. '약하다'보다 체질이 원래 약하다는 느낌이 강해서 건강 이야기에 어울려요. 팀의 수비처럼 힘이 부족한 조직에 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a body that is weak and gets sick easily. It feels more constitutional than 약하다, so it fits health talk. It can also be used figuratively for an organization lacking strength, like a team's defense.

examples.en: You look really healthy and rosy today.
I was so shocked that the color drained from my face.
Your complexion is poor and you look low on energy.
My mom checked my complexion first.

examples.ko: 혈색이 돌아온 걸 보니 다 나았나 봐요.
examples.en: Your color is back, so you must have recovered.
Just having good color makes you look much healthier.

explain: 얼굴빛이 건강해 보이는지를 말할 때 써서 '혈색이 좋다/나쁘다/돌다'가 가장 흔해요. 일상에서는 '얼굴빛'이나 '안색'이라고도 하는데, '안색'은 기분이나 건강 상태가 드러난 표정까지 포함해요.
explain_en: It describes whether your face looks healthy, most commonly as '혈색이 좋다/나쁘다/돌다'. In daily talk people also say '얼굴빛' or '안색', and '안색' also includes the look that shows mood or health.

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 환각을 본 것 같아요.
examples.en: I was so tired that I think I saw things that weren't there.

examples.ko: 오래 굶으면 환각이 보이기도 한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that if you go hungry for a long time, you can even see hallucinations.
That moment felt like a dream or a hallucination.

examples.ko: 열이 너무 높아서 환각 증상까지 나타났어요.
examples.en: The fever was so high that even hallucination symptoms appeared.

examples.ko: 인공지능이 없는 사실을 말하는 것을 환각이라고 불러요.
examples.en: When AI states facts that don't exist, it is called a hallucination.

examples.ko: 사막에서 물이 보이는 환각에 빠진 사람 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a story about a person who fell into a hallucination of seeing water in the desert.

explain: '착각'은 잘못 생각하는 것이고, '환각'은 실제로 없는 것이 보이거나 들리는 것처럼 느껴지는 거예요. 요즘은 AI가 없는 정보를 지어내는 것도 '환각'이라고 해요. '환각을 보다', '환각에 빠지다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '착각' is a mistaken idea, while '환각' is when you see or hear something that isn't really there. Nowadays it is also used for AI making up information that doesn't exist. It is used as '환각을 보다' and '환각에 빠지다'.
